newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Namibia, Indonesia agree to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: Namibia, Indonesia agree to boost trade.

text.p: Visiting Namibian President Sam Nujoma and Indonesia's President Suharto agreed on Friday to boost bilateral trade, Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said.
"The important thing is both sides wanted to expand economic cooperation and to boost trade and investment," he told reporters after talks between the two leaders.
Nujoma arrived on Thursday for a five-day visit to Indonesia. He will visit North Sumatra on Saturday and the resort island of Bali on Sunday before flying back to Namibia on Monday.
Murdiono said Namibia also wanted Indonesian investors to invest in the African nation and form joint-venture companies.
"We will seriously study the opportunities for Indonesian investors to invest there," Murdiono said.
He said Namibia also wanted expertise from Indonesia on oil and gas regulations, including production-sharing contracts.
